critique.good: The table is close to the viewport width, and all column groups appear together at first sight.
critique.problems: Names, headers and amounts break into narrow vertical fragments. Rows become very tall, making it difficult to follow one employee across the table or compare amounts down a column. The net-pay figures also split.
critique.cause: The 41–44px middle columns leave only 20–23px for text; the 50px name column and 54px net-pay column are also too narrow for their longest contents.

critique.good: The 85px net-pay column keeps the final amounts intact and gives the result a clear landing point.
critique.problems: The six component columns are almost unreadable: amounts run down as strings of individual digits, and the resulting rows are exceptionally tall. Some names also wrap. The table still requires horizontal scrolling.
critique.cause: Each 38px component column leaves only 17px for text. The 60px name column leaves 39px, less than the 46px needed for its longest name.

critique.good: Every name, header and amount stays on one line. Compact, even rows make both employee-by-employee reading and vertical comparison much easier. The earnings and deductions groups remain clear.
critique.problems: The initial viewport shows the earnings group and only part of the first deduction column; the remaining deductions and net pay require a substantial sideways scroll. The viewport boundary cuts through a column, weakening the initial view.
critique.cause: The widths preserve all contents, but the first four columns already total 308px; the 71px social-insurance column crosses the 360px viewport boundary. The full table is 618px wide.

critique.good: 姓名和所有金额保持完整；各行高度一致，应发三项在首屏内形成清楚的阅读单元。
critique.problems: 应发数值列留白偏多，首屏只能看到扣款组的一小部分，查看扣款和实发需要较多横向滚动。
critique.cause: 基本工资、绩效、补贴列分别为101、96、95px，均明显大于其内容加内边距所需宽度，合计占用了可用于首屏的空间。

critique.good: 姓名、金额和表头均未拆行；应发三列比r1A紧凑，首屏已露出扣款组及社保列，组间关系更容易察觉。
critique.problems: 社保金额被视口边界切断，读者仍须滚动才能完整核对；各金额列仍有一定富余，实发列距离首屏较远。
critique.cause: 前四列合计326px，加上表格边界后，360px视口只能容纳社保列的一部分；其余金额列也比保持内容完整所需的宽度略宽。

critique.good: 姓名和所有金额完整，行高一致；应发与扣款各列按内容需要分配宽度，表格紧凑，便于按行核对。
critique.problems: 首屏只能看到应发组和社保列的一部分；实发在视口之外，核对结果需要横向滚动。
critique.cause: 前四列共308px，第5列延伸至379px，因而被360px视口边缘切开；完整保留金额使总宽达到618px。

critique.good: 所有姓名、金额和表头保持完整，列间留白较宽，行列关系清楚。
critique.problems: 相较r2A，额外留白没有改善阅读层级，反而让首屏露出的社保内容更少，也增加了滚动距离。
critique.cause: 每列比r2A加宽4px；前四列共324px，第5列在399px处结束，总宽增至646px。

r0A.idea: 严格零滚动：按内容比例压缩全部八列，表头折成两行、金额在列内折行，用最小的横向成本换取一屏内看到完整对照。

r0B.idea: 结果优先的非对称方案：把宽度让给姓名和实发，让“谁、拿多少”永不折断，中间六个应发/扣款列收窄承担折行代价。

r0C.idea: 不折任何数字：每列给足其最长金额的原生宽度，首屏只露出姓名、基本工资、绩效和部分补贴，其余靠横向滚动换取完整可读的金额。

r1A.idea: Keep every value intact and widen the three earnings columns so the name and complete earnings group total 359px. The initial view ends at a meaningful group boundary; deductions and net pay remain available by scrolling. The tradeoff is a wider 668px table.

r1B.idea: Refine r0C with 6px of extra room in each numeric column, preserving its compact, single-line rows while giving amounts more breathing room. The 659px table requires more scrolling, and the viewport still cuts through the first deduction column.

r2A.idea: 按各列最长内容加21px配置宽度，保留人名、金额和表头完整。总宽617px，比r1B缩短43px；首屏更充分地呈现社保列，并减少查看实发所需的滚动。

r2B.idea: 在内容完整的最低宽度基础上，为各金额列各增加4px，保留较舒展的数值带和结果列。总宽645px，在横向滚动量与列间呼吸感之间取折中。

r3A.idea: 以r2A为基础加宽应发三列，使姓名与完整应发组恰好占359px；首屏在组边界结束，避免社保列被截断，同时保持所有金额完整。代价是总宽增至669px，查看扣款和实发需要滚动更远。

understanding.purpose: 一张中文月度工资条：6名员工，展示应发三项（基本工资、绩效、补贴）、扣款三项（社保、公积金、个税）以及最终实发金额；读者用它核对每人工资的构成、逐项相减是否成立，并比较实发金额。
understanding.reading: 按行读：先看姓名，再从左到右看应发各项、扣款各项，最后落到实发；同时也会纵向扫某一列（如个税或实发）找异常。姓名是定位点，实发是阅读终点，中间的六个金额列是同质的“数值带”。
groups: 第1列 姓名：行的锚点，必须与数据行对齐，属于独立角色
第2–4列 应发（基本工资、绩效、补贴）：同组，需要彼此可比、视觉权重一致
第5–7列 扣款（社保、公积金、个税）：同组，与应发组并列、权重一致
第8列 实发：结果列，应与中间六列区分开，宽度和留白上更像“落点”
keep_intact: 姓名（2–3字人名不应拆行，否则整行定位失效）
实发金额（每行结论，含两位小数，绝不能断开）
所有金额的整数与小数部分（8600.00 若断成 8600. / 00 就失去可读性与小数对齐）
may_wrap: 四字子表头（基本工资、公积金等）可折成 2+2，表头行本就有两层高度可吸收
姓名列若收窄，人名可折成两行，行高有余量
补贴、社保这类较短金额列（如 600.00、688.00）在极窄时可退让

bad.why: Names, headers, and nearly every monetary amount split across lines, making rows and figures difficult to scan.
The narrow middle columns break amounts into as many as six lines, producing very tall rows while the table still overflows the viewport.

final.rationale: r0C and r2A are identical and keep every name, header, and amount on one line while using the least horizontal space among the intact candidates. The initial viewport shows the employee and all three earnings columns, with the deductions group beginning at the right edge. Scrolling is needed to compare deductions and net pay, but the compact, even rows preserve those figures and their relationships.

general: Keep monetary amounts intact so readers can compare values without reconstructing digits across lines.
Give related columns a consistent rhythm while allowing widths to reflect their content.
Judge horizontal scrolling against the readability of the full table and the information visible initially.
specific: The first viewport can show the name and the complete earnings group, with the start of deductions signaling further content.
The preferred widths are close to the minimum needed to keep this table's headers and values on one line.

final.tradeoffs: Wider candidates give cells more breathing room, but require more scrolling and reveal less of the deductions group initially. Squeezing into the viewport avoids scrolling at the cost of severely fragmented amounts.
final.uncertain: A designer might prefer the extra space in r2B or the wider earnings columns in r1A and r3A; the ranges are approximate judgments of equivalent quality, not measured rendering thresholds.

A.why: Names and earnings remain intact, with compact rows and a clear grouped header. Most deductions and net pay require horizontal scrolling.

B.why: All columns fit initially, but names, headers and nearly every amount are broken across several lines, making comparisons difficult.

C.why: Amounts in the visible earnings columns stay intact, but the narrow name column splits names vertically and makes rows unnecessarily tall. Deductions and net pay still require scrolling.

D.why: The full table fits, but amounts are fragmented into multiple lines throughout, including net pay. The resulting tall rows are hard to scan.

E.why: Names and visible earnings amounts are intact and easy to read, but generous column widths leave deductions almost entirely beyond the initial viewport and increase the scrolling needed.

F.why: Names and visible amounts stay intact in compact rows. The earnings group and part of deductions appear initially, though the remaining deductions and net pay require scrolling.

reviews.unsure: The screenshots do not show the full widths or contents of columns beyond their right edges, so the total scrolling distance and the rendering of those columns cannot be assessed fully.

A.why: Names and amounts stay intact, and the full 应发 group fits cleanly within the viewport. Readers must scroll to see deductions and take-home pay.

B.why: Names and earnings remain readable, and the 扣款 group begins in view, but the 社保 amounts are cut by the viewport edge and require scrolling to read.

C.why: The whole table fits, but names, headers and nearly every amount are broken across multiple lines, making rows and comparisons difficult to follow.

D.why: Amounts stay intact, but the narrow name column splits every name vertically and makes rows unusually tall. The remaining columns still require horizontal scrolling.

E.why: All columns fit, but names and monetary amounts split across several lines, with inconsistent breaks that make values hard to reconstruct and compare.

F.why: Names and earnings stay intact with clear rows, but the viewport cuts through the 扣款 group and its first column, leaving the rest to horizontal scrolling.
